items.en: The Marks of External Wholesome Roots Arising
items.zh: 正明善根發相 · 外善根發相

zh: 第二、次明善根發相，亦還為二：一、明外善根發相；二、明內善根發相。云何外善根發相？外善非一，今依前章門略出五種：
en: Second, next clarifying the marks of wholesome roots arising: this too has two parts — clarifying the marks of external wholesome roots arising, and clarifying the marks of internal wholesome roots arising. What, then, are the marks of external wholesome roots arising? External wholesomeness is not of one kind only; here, following the topics already given above, five kinds are set out in brief:

zh: 初、明行者若坐中靜定，忽見種種衣服、臥具、飲食、珍寶、田園、池沼、車乘。如是等事，或復因心靜故，自能捨離慳貪，心行惠施，無所悋惜。當知此是過去、今生布施，習、報二種善根發相。
en: First: if, while the practitioner sits in still concentration, various sorts of clothing, bedding, food and drink, treasures, fields and gardens, ponds, or carriages suddenly appear — or if, because the mind is still, one becomes able of oneself to let go of stinginess and greed, the mind moving toward generosity, giving without any reluctance — one should know that this is the mark of the two kinds of wholesome roots, from habituation and from retribution, arising through giving in the past and in this present life.

zh: 二、行者若於止靜定之中，忽見自身相好端嚴，身所著衣清淨如法，洗浴清潔，得好淨物。見如是等事，或復因心靜故，發戒忍心，自然知輕識重，乃至小罪，心生怖畏，忍辱謙卑。當知此是過去、今生戒忍，習、報二種善根發相也。
en: Second: if the practitioner, within stopping and still concentration, suddenly sees their own body handsome and dignified in form, the robes they wear pure and in accordance with the Dharma, freshly bathed and clean, obtaining fine, pure things — or if, because the mind is still, precept-observance and patience arise within the mind, so that one naturally distinguishes the light offense from the grave, and even at the slightest offense the mind grows fearful, forbearing and humble — one should know that this, too, is the mark of the two kinds of wholesome roots, from habituation and from retribution, arising through precepts and patience in the past and in this present life.

zh: 三、行者若於坐中，忽見師僧、父母、宗親、眷屬著淨衣服，歡喜悅豫端嚴。見如是等事，或復以心靜故，自然慈仁、恭敬、孝悌心生。當知此是過去、今生孝順尊長，習、報二種善根發相也。
en: Third: if the practitioner, while sitting, suddenly sees teachers and monastics, parents, relatives, and family members wearing pure clothing, joyful, content, and dignified — or if, because the mind is still, kindness, reverence, filial devotion, and brotherly respect arise naturally within the mind — one should know that this, too, is the mark of the two kinds of wholesome roots, from habituation and from retribution, arising through filial devotion toward one's elders in the past and in this present life.

zh: 四、行者若於坐中，忽見諸塔寺、尊儀形像、經書、供養莊嚴清淨僧眾雲集法會。見如是等事，或復於靜心中發信敬，尊重三寶，心樂供養，精勤勇猛，常無懈倦。當知此是過去、今生信敬三寶，精勤供養，習、報二種善根發相也。
en: Fourth: if the practitioner, while sitting, suddenly sees stūpas and temples, revered images, sūtra texts, or a pure assembly of monastics gathered for a dharma-assembly, with offerings adorned and solemn — or if, within the still mind, faith and reverence arise, honoring the Triple Gem, the mind delighting in making offerings, diligent and vigorous, never growing weary — one should know that this, too, is the mark of the two kinds of wholesome roots, from habituation and from retribution, arising through faith and reverence toward the Triple Gem, together with diligent offering, in the past and in this present life.

zh: 五、行者若於坐中，因心澄靜，或見解釋三藏、聽受讀誦大乘有德四眾；或時因心靜故，讀誦自然而入，隨所聽聞，即時開悟，或復自然能了解三藏大乘經典，分別無滯。當知悉是過去、今生讀誦聽說，習、報二種善根發相。
en: Fifth: if the practitioner, while sitting, because the mind is clear and still, sees virtuous members of the four assemblies expounding the Tripiṭaka, or listening to, receiving, and reciting the Mahāyāna — or if, at times, because the mind is still, reading and reciting come naturally and easily, so that whatever is heard is understood at once, or one is naturally able to comprehend the Tripiṭaka and the Mahāyāna sūtras, distinguishing their meaning without any obstruction — one should know that all of this is the mark of the two kinds of wholesome roots, from habituation and from retribution, arising through reading, reciting, listening, and expounding in the past and in this present life.

zh: 行者見如是種種好相，及發諸善心者，此非禪定，多是過去、今生於散心中修諸功德，今以心靜力故，得發其事，見諸相貌，悉屬報因相現，善心開發，皆是習因善發也。如是眾多，說不可盡，此則略示大意。
en: When the practitioner sees such various favorable marks as these, and wholesome states of mind are brought forth, this is not itself dhyāna-concentration — for the most part it is merit cultivated within a scattered mind in the past and in this present life, now brought forth through the power of the stilled mind: the various appearances seen all belong to the manifestation of the retribution-cause, while the arising of wholesome mind is, in every case, the arising of the habituation-cause. Such cases are many and cannot be exhaustively described; this, in brief, indicates only the general sense of it.

zh: 復次，發習、報兩因，行人根性不同，自有行人但發報因相，不發習因善心；自有行人但發習因善心，而不發報因之相；自有行人具發習、報兩因；自有行人二俱不發。如是等事，因緣難解，豈可謬釋？
en: Furthermore: in the arising of the two causes, habituation and retribution, practitioners' capacities differ. Some practitioners bring forth only the mark of the retribution-cause, without bringing forth the wholesome mind of the habituation-cause; some bring forth only the wholesome mind of the habituation-cause, without bringing forth the mark of the retribution-cause; some bring forth both causes, habituation and retribution, together; and some bring forth neither. Matters such as these, bound up in causes and conditions difficult to fathom, could hardly be explained through careless guesswork.

zh: 問曰：散心善根，何得於靜心中現？答曰：於禪定中尚得見過去、今生所起煩惱惡業，何況善根扶理而不得見？
en: Question: how can wholesome roots cultivated with a scattered mind manifest within a still mind? Answer: within dhyāna-concentration, one can even see the afflictions and unwholesome karmic actions arisen in the past and in this present life — how much more, then, can wholesome roots, which accord with principle, fail to be seen?

zh: 問曰：見此等諸相，亦有是魔所作不？答曰：亦有是魔所作。若欲分別，但魔名殺者。若此等相發時，能令行人心識動亂，或復增諸煩惱，逼迫障蔽，眾多妨難，不利定心，悉是魔之所作。其善根發者，行人自覺，見此相已，雖復未證禪定，而身心明白，諸根清淨，身有色力，所為吉利，善念開發，因此已後，自覺心神易可攝錄，身心安隱，無諸過患。當知此為善根發相。
en: Question: among such marks as these that are seen, is it also possible that some are the work of demons? Answer: yes, some are indeed the work of demons. If one wishes to distinguish them: a demon, simply put, is named "the killer." Whenever such marks as these arise and cause the practitioner's mind and consciousness to become agitated and disordered, or cause afflictions to increase, pressing in and obstructing, bringing many hindrances and obstacles that are of no benefit to the concentrated mind — all of this is the work of a demon. As for the arising of a genuine wholesome root: the practitioner becomes aware of it directly, and, upon seeing such a mark, although dhyāna-concentration is not yet realized, body and mind become clear and bright, the faculties become pure, the body gains vigor and color, what one undertakes turns out well, and wholesome thoughts are brought forth; from this point on, one becomes aware that the mind and spirit are easily gathered in, body and mind are at peace, and free of any fault. One should know that this is the mark of a wholesome root arising.

zh: 復次，若此等事，善根發者，報因之相則暫現便謝，習因心善則相續不斷。若是魔作相，則久久不滅，雖謝更來，逼亂行者，善心則暫發還滅，或時變成惡念，當知邪也。復次，邪正之相甚為難測，自非親近明師，非可妄取。
en: Furthermore: in such matters as these, when it is a genuine wholesome root arising, the mark of the retribution-cause appears only briefly and then passes away, while the wholesome mind of the habituation-cause continues on without interruption. But if it is a mark made by a demon, it fails to disappear for a very long time, and even once it passes, it returns again, pressing in and disturbing the practitioner — the wholesome mind arises only briefly and then vanishes again, and at times even turns into an unwholesome thought; one should know that this is deviant. Furthermore, the marks of the deviant and the correct are extremely difficult to fathom — without drawing close to an enlightened teacher, one should not presume to judge them for oneself.

zh: 問曰：此諸善根為當一向前發，亦得證諸禪時於深定中發也？答曰：此事無定，未必一向定前見也。外善既麁，故先明耳。
en: Question: do these wholesome roots always arise beforehand, or can they also arise within deep concentration, at the very time the various dhyānas are actually realized? Answer: this is not fixed either way — it is not necessarily the case that they are always seen only prior to concentration. It is simply that external wholesomeness is the coarser of the two, and so it has been clarified first.

The recurring pair here — the habituation-cause (習因) and the retribution-cause (報因) — distinguishes two things that can look identical from the inside: a vivid mental image of, say, fine robes or a solemn temple (the retribution-cause, a mark surfacing from past karma) versus the actual wholesome disposition that arises alongside it, such as spontaneous generosity or reverence (the habituation-cause, the trace of past cultivation now resuming). The treatise's answer to "how do I know this isn't a demon?" is notably practical rather than doctrinal: genuine wholesome marks are brief and self-limiting while the wholesome mind-state they leave behind persists; demonic marks are persistent and recurring while the wholesome mind-state they produce is fragile and quick to collapse, sometimes into its opposite. This is the treatise's first extended treatment of demonic interference — worth remembering once the fifth internal-expedient-means layer, recognizing demonic affairs (覺魔事), is reached later in the treatise.

items.en: The Marks of Internal Wholesome Roots Arising: Mindfulness of the Breath
items.zh: 內善根發相 · 阿那波那門

zh: 第二、云何名內善根發相？今約五門禪中辨內善根發。此五門中，一門開為三，合有十五種善根發：一、明阿那波那門有三種善根發相不同：一、數息善根；二、隨息善根；三、觀息善根。
en: Second, what is meant by the marks of internal wholesome roots arising? Here, internal wholesome roots arising is distinguished with reference to the five-gate dhyāna. Within these five gates, each gate opens into three, giving fifteen kinds of wholesome roots arising in all. First, clarifying that the gate of mindfulness of the breath has three differing marks of wholesome roots arising: the wholesome root of counting the breath; the wholesome root of following the breath; and the wholesome root of contemplating the breath.

zh: 一、數息善根者，行人如上善修三止，身心調和，發於欲界及未到地等諸禪，身心湛然空寂，定心安隱，於後或一坐二坐，乃至經旬，或經月經年，將息得所，定心不退，即於定中，心忽覺身心運動，八觸次第而起，此即發根本初禪善根之相。於此定中，喜樂善心安隱不可為諭。如是發初禪已，乃至發四禪定空等。
en: First, the wholesome root of counting the breath: the practitioner, skillfully cultivating the three kinds of stopping as given above, body and mind harmonized, brings forth the dhyānas of the desire realm and the "not-yet-arrived" state; body and mind become deep and empty, still, and the concentrated mind at peace. Afterward, whether in one sitting, two sittings, or over the course of ten days, a month, or a year, once rest is properly regulated and the concentrated mind no longer regresses, then, within concentration, the mind suddenly becomes aware of body and mind in motion, and the eight tactile sensations arise one after another in sequence — this is precisely the mark of the wholesome root of the root first dhyāna arising. Within this concentration, joy, happiness, and a wholesome, peaceful mind arise beyond what words can convey. Having thus brought forth the first dhyāna, one goes on to bring forth the second, third, and fourth dhyānas, the formless attainments, and the rest.

zh: 二、隨息善根發，亦於欲界、未到靜定心中，忽然覺息出入長短，及遍身毛孔虛疎，即以心明見於身內三十六物，猶如開倉見穀、粟、麻、荳等，心大驚喜，寂靜安快，除諸身行，乃至心受喜樂等，是為特勝善根發相。
en: Second, the arising of the wholesome root of following the breath: likewise, within the still concentration of the desire realm and the "not-yet-arrived" state, one suddenly becomes aware of the breath going out and in, long or short, and of every pore of the body open and porous; the mind then clearly sees the thirty-six substances within the body, just as one might open a granary and see grain, millet, hemp-seed, and beans — the mind is greatly astonished and delighted, still and at ease, every bodily formation set to rest, feeling joy and happiness and the rest. This is the mark of the special-excellences dhyāna's wholesome root arising.

zh: 三、明觀息善根發者，亦於欲界、未到細靜心中，忽見自身氣息從毛孔出入，遍身無礙，漸漸明利，如羅縠中見皮重數乃至骨肉等亦如是；亦見身內八萬戶蟲麁細長短，言語音聲，定心喜樂，倍於上說，或見自身猶如芭蕉、聚沫、雲影相等。此是通明觀善根發相。
en: Third, clarifying the arising of the wholesome root of contemplating the breath: likewise, within the fine, still mind of the desire realm and the "not-yet-arrived" state, one suddenly sees one's own breath going out and in through every pore, unobstructed throughout the body, growing gradually clearer and sharper, as though seeing, through a fine silk gauze, the layered skin, and, in the same way, the flesh and bones beneath; one also sees the eighty thousand households of worms within the body, coarse and fine, long and short, along with their speech and sound, the concentrated mind's joy and happiness doubled beyond what was said above; or one sees one's own body as though it were a plantain trunk, a mass of foam, or the reflection of a cloud. This is the mark of the thorough-and-bright contemplation's wholesome root arising.

These three marks recapitulate, in order of increasing subtlety, the three breath-based attainments fascicle 2 already named in passing: the root dhyānas from bare counting of the breath, the sixteen special excellences from following it, and the thorough-and-bright contemplation from directly contemplating it — each gate's arising-mark growing more penetrating than the last, from the eight tactile sensations of ordinary absorption to a vision of the body dissolving into its ultimate constituents, down to the parasitic life the treatise says inhabits it.

quiz.q: In the first mark of external wholesome roots, giving, what may one see while sitting?
options: teachers and parents in pure clothing
one's own body handsome and dignified
clothing, bedding, food, treasures, fields, ponds, carriages — or one naturally lets go of stinginess and gives freely
quiz.why: "Various sorts of clothing, bedding, food and drink, treasures, fields and gardens, ponds, or carriages suddenly appear — or if, because the mind is still, one becomes able of oneself to let go of stinginess and greed ... this is the mark of the two kinds of wholesome roots ... arising through giving." The others are the marks for precepts, filial devotion, and faith.

quiz.q: Seeing favorable marks and giving rise to wholesome minds — is this dhyāna? To which cause do the marks and the mind belong?
options: not dhyāna; merit from scattered-mind practice brought forth by stillness; the marks are retribution-cause, the wholesome mind habituation-cause
quiz.why: "This is not itself dhyāna-concentration — for the most part it is merit cultivated within a scattered mind ... the various appearances seen all belong to the manifestation of the retribution-cause, while the arising of wholesome mind is, in every case, the arising of the habituation-cause."

quiz.q: How can wholesome roots cultivated with a scattered mind appear in a still mind?
options: in concentration even past afflictions and evil karma can be seen — how much more wholesome roots, which accord with principle
quiz.why: "Within dhyāna-concentration, one can even see the afflictions and unwholesome karmic actions arisen in the past and in this present life — how much more, then, can wholesome roots, which accord with principle, fail to be seen?"

quiz.q: If such marks are the work of a demon, how are they distinguished?
options: good marks are wholesome, bad ones demonic
a demon is "the killer": marks that agitate the mind, increase affliction, and obstruct concentration are demonic; a wholesome root brings clarity, pure faculties, and an easily gathered mind
demonic marks never appear in sitting
quiz.why: "A demon, simply put, is named 'the killer.' Whenever such marks as these arise and cause the practitioner's mind and consciousness to become agitated and disordered, or cause afflictions to increase ... all of this is the work of a demon." A wholesome root leaves body and mind clear and the mind easily gathered. The test is the effect, not whether the mark looks good.

quiz.q: How do a wholesome root and a demonic mark differ in how long they last?
options: wholesome: the retribution mark appears briefly, the habituation mind continues; demonic: the mark lingers or returns, and the wholesome mind soon vanishes
quiz.why: "When it is a genuine wholesome root arising, the mark of the retribution-cause appears only briefly and then passes away, while the wholesome mind of the habituation-cause continues on without interruption. But if it is a mark made by a demon, it fails to disappear for a very long time, and even once it passes, it returns again."

quiz.q: How many kinds of internal wholesome roots arising are there, and how are they counted?
options: each of the five gates opens into three, fifteen in all
quiz.why: "Within these five gates, each gate opens into three, giving fifteen kinds of wholesome roots arising in all."

quiz.q: What marks the arising of the wholesome root of counting the breath?
options: in concentration one suddenly feels body and mind move, the eight tactile sensations arising in sequence — the mark of the root first dhyāna
seeing the breath through the pores
quiz.why: "Within concentration, the mind suddenly becomes aware of body and mind in motion, and the eight tactile sensations arise one after another in sequence — this is precisely the mark of the wholesome root of the root first dhyāna arising." The others are following the breath, contemplating the breath, and the nine contemplations.

quiz.q: When the wholesome root of following the breath arises and one sees the thirty-six substances, what is it likened to, and which dhyāna is it?
options: like a plantain and foam; nine contemplations
like opening a granary and seeing grain, millet, hemp, beans; the special-excellences dhyāna
like still water; the five wheels
quiz.why: "The mind then clearly sees the thirty-six substances within the body, just as one might open a granary and see grain, millet, hemp-seed, and beans ... This is the mark of the special-excellences dhyāna's wholesome root arising." The gauze and the plantain belong to contemplating the breath.

quiz.q: The wholesome root of contemplating the breath belongs to which dhyāna, and what are its features?
options: the root first dhyāna: eight sensations
thorough-and-bright: the breath through every pore, seeing skin and bone as through gauze, the eighty thousand households of worms, the body like a plantain, foam, a cloud's reflection
quiz.why: "One suddenly sees one's own breath going out and in through every pore ... as though seeing, through a fine silk gauze, the layered skin ... one also sees the eighty thousand households of worms within the body ... or one sees one's own body as though it were a plantain trunk, a mass of foam, or the reflection of a cloud. This is the mark of the thorough-and-bright contemplation's wholesome root arising."

quiz.q: Do wholesome roots always arise before dhyāna is realized, and why was external wholesomeness explained first?
options: always before; external is more important
not fixed; not always seen before concentration; external wholesomeness is coarser, so it is explained first
quiz.why: "This is not fixed either way — it is not necessarily the case that they are always seen only prior to concentration. It is simply that external wholesomeness is the coarser of the two, and so it has been clarified first."
